spells.name: Blessed Padding
spells.description:
You target one creature you can see within range, attempting to overwhelm them with a sudden, disruptive impulse. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or immediately use its reaction to perform one of the following harmless, chaotic acts (your choice):
- Drop one item it is holding.
- Fall prone.
  - Use all of its remaining movement to run in a random direction.
  - Use their diaper if wearing one, or soil their pants (need dependent).

spells.name: Clutching Shadows
spells.description:
You cause the shadows around a creature to writhe and grasp. Choose one creature you can see within range. The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be restrained by the shadows for the duration. At the start of each of its turns, the target can repeat the saving throw, ending the effect on a success. While restrained, the creature perceives the shadows as monstrous, grasping claws and is considered frightened of you.
Monster in the Closet 3rd-level conjuration

spells.name: Crinkly Invitation

components.material: a small, decorative bow or plastic fastener

spells.description:
You create a subtle, magically enticing crinkling sound either by shaking your hips or rubbing your diapered butt- only one creature of your choice within range can hear this sound by these magical means. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be captivated by the sound. On a failed save, the creature is compelled to use all of its available movement on its next turn to move closer to you by the safest route available. The creature does nothing on its turn except move.
Padding Perfection 2nd-level transmutation

spells.name: Embarrassment
spells.description:
You choose one creature you can see within range. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be overcome with intense magical embarrassment.
While affected, the creature has disadvantage on all attack rolls and ability checks as it is too flustered to act effectively. If the target fails a check on their next turn, including a check to attempt to negate or resist the effects of the spell, they must make a potty check at disadvantage. The spell ends early if the target takes damage.

spells.name: Forced Incontinence
spells.description: Choose a creature you can see within range. The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or lose control of its bodily functions for the duration. At the start of each of its turns, the target automatically fails a diaper check if it is wearing a diaper. If it is not, it soils its clothing, and its speed is halved for that turn due to the discomfort and distraction.

spells.name: Gold Star of Approval
spells.description: You choose one willing creature you can see within range. A shimmering, golden star sticker appears on their forehead. For the duration, whenever the creature uses its action to perform a helpful, non-damaging act (such as casting a healing spell, using the Help action, or stabilizing a creature), it gains temporary hit points equal to your spellcasting ability modifier. The spell ends if the creature deals damage to another creature.

spells.name: Imprint

components.material: a small, blank piece of fabric

spells.description:
You attempt to trap a foe as a harmless decoration on your own diaper. Choose one creature you can see within range. The target must succeed on a Charisma saving throw or be magically transformed into a two-dimensional image and imprinted onto the front- or butt-of the diaper you are currently wearing.
While imprinted, the target is incapacitated and has total cover. The effect ends if your concentration is broken, if you or the target move more than 120 feet apart, or if you dismiss it (no action required).
Whenever your diaper expends a use charge (due to a failed Continence Check or other effect), the imprinted creature takes 1d10 psychic damage at the end of that turn, as the magical filth seeps into their patterned form. If you purposefully fail a Continence Check while a creature is imprinted, this damage is doubled to 2d10.
Creatures reduced to zero hit points in this fashion are permanently affixed to the diaper and cannot be resurrected except with the use of True Resurrection, Wish, or Miracle.
Masterwork Diaper 5th-level conjuration

spells.name: Padded Sanctuary
spells.description: You create a field of regressive energy around you. Each hostile creature that starts its turn in the area must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become magically suggestible and childlike. An affected creature can't take reactions and must use its action to perform a harmless, childish activity, such as sucking its thumb, babbling incoherently, or sitting down and crying.

If the creature sleeps for the full duration, it awakens feeling refreshed and gains 2d8+5 temporary hit points.

On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and its action is not affected. For the duration of the spell, as a bonus action on your turn, you can force the creature to take an additional 1d8 psychic damage as long as it is within 30 feet of a shadow. spells.name: Study Hall
spells.description:
You create a zone of intense academic focus around you. A 30-foot-radius sphere, filled with the faint, spectral images of library shelves, extends from you. The area is under the effect of a silence spell.
  Additionally, any friendly creature that spends its turn inside the sphere doing nothing but concentrating on a spell has advantage on Constitution saving throws to maintain concentration until the start of their next turn.

Detention Field
disciplinary energy. Choose a creature you can see within range. The target must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is restrained for the duration by shimmering, golden lines of magic that form a 5-foot cube around it.
  As an action, the restrained creature can make a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC, breaking free on a success.
spells.higherlevels:
When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you can target one additional creature for each slot level above 2nd.
Enforced Mandate

No Running in the Halls. An affected creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have its speed halved. If it attempts to use the Dash action, it immediately falls prone.
Raise Your Hand to Speak. An affected creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be unable to speak or provide verbal spell components unless it first uses its bonus action to raise its hand. Keep Your Hands to Yourself. An affected creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become unable to make melee attacks against other creatures.
  At the end of each of its turns, an affected creature can repeat its saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Summon Proctor
  You summon a spectral proctor from the Academy's spirit. The proctor appears in an unoccupied space you can see. It uses the veteran stat block, but it is a construct, its weapon attacks are magical, and they deal force damage.
  The proctor is friendly to you and your companions and follows your verbal commands, acting on its own initiative. Its primary purpose is to enforce order and protect students. It will not cause lethal harm unless specifically commanded to against a clear, dangerous threat.
  If you lose concentration, the proctor acts on its own to restore order for 1 minute before vanishing.
Plagiarize
  You attempt to magically copy knowledge from another spellcaster. Target a creature you can see within range that is capable of casting spells. The target must make an Intelligence saving throw.
  On a failed save, you choose one spell of 3rd level or lower from the target's spell list. For the next 8 hours, you know this spell, and it counts as a sorcerer spell for you. You can cast it using your spell slots.
  The target does not lose the spell, but is aware of the theft on a successful save.
Examination Dread
  You instill the paralyzing fear of a surprise final exam in a creature's mind. Target one creature you can see. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw.
  On a failure, the creature becomes frightened of you. While frightened, at the start of each of its turns, the creature must use its action to frantically answer a spectral test paper that appears before it, preventing it from taking any other action.
  At the end of each of its turns, the creature can repeat the saving throw, ending the effect on a success.

Manifest Curriculum
  You pull the principles of an academic subject into reality, altering the area in a 30-foot cube centered on yourself. Choose one of the following subjects:

Geometry. The ground becomes a confusing grid of shifting lines and angles, creating difficult terrain.
Any creature ending its turn in the area must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take 4d6 force damage.
Alchemy. Vials of volatile chemicals bubble up from the ground. Any creature that enters the area or starts its turn there must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or take 4d8 acid or fire damage (your choice).
Conjuration Theory. The area becomes a nexus of unstable portals. Any creature ending its turn in the area must succeed on a Charisma saving throw or be randomly teleported to an unoccupied space within 30 feet.
Expel
  You issue a magical decree of expulsion against one creature. The target must succeed on a Charisma saving throw or be banished to a harmless demiplane.
  At the end of the target's next turn, it reappears in the space it left. However, the shame of its expulsion lingers. For the next minute, the target has disadvantage on all attack rolls and ability checks.

Sorcerous Origin: Entropic Pampath

ot all magic comes from ancient bloodlines or pacts with powerful entities. Some sorcerers are simply born with a direct connection to the raw, untamed chaos of emotion itself. An Entropic Pampath's power is the arcane equivalent of a toddler's meltdown:
explosive, unpredictable, and capable of bending reality to their whims. These sorcerers don't study or bargain for their magic; they feel it, deeply and intensely.
Frustration can cause toys to animate and attack, a stubbed toe can unleash a wave of debilitating despair, and a fit of giggles can fill the air with illusory butterflies. For an Entropic Pampath, magic isn't a tool
-it's an outburst, a primal scream of emotion that the world has no choice but to obey.
Entropic Pampath Spells

Sorcerer Level

Tantrum Magic
Starting at 1st level, your spellcasting can unleash surges of untamed magic. Immediately after you cast a sorcerer spell of 1st level or higher, the DM can have you roll a d20. If you roll a 1, roll on the Wild Magic Tantrum Table to create a random magical effect.

Temperamental Control
Also at 1st level, you can tap into your wild emotions to gain a momentary edge. You can gain advantage on one attack roll, ability check, or saving throw. You must finish a long rest before you can use this feature again.
  Any time before you regain the use of this feature, the DM can have you roll on the Wild Magic Tantrum Table immediately after you cast a sorcerer spell of 1st level or higher. You then regain the use of this feature.
Lineage Spells
You learn additional spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown on the Entropic Pampath Spells table. Each of these spells counts as a sorcerer spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of sorcerer spells you know. These spells can't be replaced when you gain a level in this class.
Bratty Interjection
Starting at 6th level, you have the ability to weaponize your fickle mood swings to affect others. When another creature you can see makes an attack roll, an ability check, or a saving throw, you can use your reaction and spend 2 sorcery points to roll a d4 and apply the number rolled as a bonus or penalty (your choice) to the creature's roll. You can do so after the creature rolls but before any effects of the roll occur.
Unleashed Tantrum
Starting at 14th level, you can unleash a wave of overwhelming, chaotic emotion. As an action, you can expend 4 sorcery points to force each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you to make a Wisdom saving throw against your sorcerer spell save DC.
  On a failed save, a creature is affected by the Confusion spell for 1 minute. This effect doesn't require your concentration. Additionally, any creature that fails its initial saving throw is overwhelmed by the emotional force and must immediately make a potty check. At the end of each of its turns, an affected creature can repeat the Wisdom saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success.
Temper Tantrum Incarnate
At 18th level, your emotional outbursts can temporarily unravel the laws of reality around you. As a bonus action, you can spend 6 sorcery points to become an avatar of chaos for 1 minute. For the duration, you roll on the Wild Magic Tantrum table at the start of each of your turns. Furthermore, whenever you roll on the Wild Magic Tantrum table, you can roll the d100 twice and use either number.

Entropic Pampath Spell Descriptions
Tantrum Bolt
  You unleash a bolt of raw, chaotic emotion at a creature you can see. Make a ranged spell attack. On a hit, the target takes 3d8 psychic damage. The chaotic nature of the bolt then causes a secondary effect. Roll a d4 to determine the effect:

1. Anger. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or use its reaction to make one melee weapon attack against a creature of your choice within its reach.
2. Sadness. The target is overcome with sorrow and has its speed halved until the end of its next turn.
3. Fear. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become frightened of you until the end of its next turn.
4. Joy. The target is struck by a fit of giggles and must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or fall prone.
When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the damage increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 1st.
Glittergloom
  You cause a 20-foot-radius sphere of swirling particles to appear, centered on a point you choose within range. You decide if it is glitter or gloom.

Glitter. The sphere is filled with dazzling, distracting glitter. The area is heavily obscured. Any creature that ends its turn in the area must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be blinded until the end of its next turn.
Gloom. The sphere is filled with shadowy, unsettling shapes. The area is filled with magical darkness. Any creature that ends its turn in the area must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be frightened of the darkness until the end of its next turn.

Animate Toy
  Your magic infuses a toy with a semblance of life. The toy becomes a creature under your control and uses the Animated Toy stat block. It acts on its own initiative. As a bonus action, you can mentally command the toy if it is within 60 feet of you. If you issue no commands, it defends itself from hostile creatures but otherwise takes no actions.

Wail of Despair
  You let out a magically potent wail of pure misery. Each creature in a 30-foot cone must make a Wisdom saving throw. A creature takes 3d8 psychic damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.
  A creature that fails its save is also overcome by despair and cannot take reactions until the start of its next turn.
When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the damage increases by 1d8 for each slot level above 2nd.

Crayon Reality
  You flourish a magical crayon and sketch a simple, two-dimensional object onto a solid surface. The drawing then springs into a three-dimensional, semi- real form. You can create one of the following effects:

Wall. You create a solid-looking crayon wall that is up to 30 feet long, 10 feet high, and 1 foot thick. The wall has an AC of 10 and 20 hit points. It provides total cover.
Goo. You draw a puddle that becomes a 15-foot square of sticky goo on the ground. The area is difficult terrain, and any creature that starts its turn there must succeed on a Strength saving throw or have its speed reduced to 0 until the start of its next turn.
Bounce Pad. You draw a 10-foot square that becomes a bouncy surface. Any creature that enters the area can choose to be launched 20 feet into the air in a direction of their choice, landing safely.
Stompy Foot
  You stomp your foot with magical force, creating a shockwave. Each creature on the ground within a 20- foot radius of you must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 4d10 bludgeoning damage and is knocked prone. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and isn't knocked prone.
Emotional Cascade
  You flood a creature's mind with overwhelming emotion. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be affected by the spell. Roll a d4 at the start of each of the affected creature's turns to determine its emotional state:
1. Rage. The creature must use its action to make a melee attack against the nearest creature.
2. 
Despair. The creature is incapacitated and must use its movement to crawl into the nearest unoccupied space that provides cover, if available.
3. Hysteria. The creature is stunned by uncontrollable laughter or crying.
4. Bliss. The creature is charmed by every other creature it can see.
  At the end of each of its turns, the target can make another Wisdom saving throw. On a success, the spell ends.
Imaginary Friend
  You summon a faintly shimmering, translucent guardian that looks like a fantastical creature from a child's imagination. It floats around you and provides protection.
  For the duration, whenever a creature you can see attacks you, your imaginary friend can use its reaction to impose disadvantage on the attack roll.
Reality Meltdown
  You unleash your emotions, causing reality itself to throw a tantrum in a 30-foot radius around you. The area becomes difficult terrain.
  When a creature enters the spell's area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, it must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be subject to a random chaotic effect. Roll a d6:
1. The creature takes 4d10 force damage.
2. The creature is teleported to an unoccupied space of your choice within the area.
3. The creature is restrained by sticky, colorful goo until the start of its next turn.
4. The creature is polymorphed into a harmless plush toy (as the polymorph spell) until the start of its next turn.
5. A shower of sparks erupts from the creature. It and each creature within 10 feet of it take 3d6 fire damage.
6. The creature is launched 30 feet straight up into the air and lands prone, taking falling damage as normal.

It's MINE!
  You fixate on an object or creature with possessive desire. Choose one creature or one object that is not being worn or carried within range.

Creature. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or be charmed by you for the duration. While charmed, the creature sees you as its most treasured person and will use its turns to protect you from any perceived threat. It will not willingly move more than 30 feet away from you.
Object. You gain telekinetic control over the object for the duration. As a bonus action on your turn, you can move the object up to 30 feet and make a single melee spell attack against a creature within 5 feet of it. On a hit, the target takes 4d12 force damage.
  At the end of each of its turns, an affected creature can repeat its saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Padded Magic for All!
Step into a world where the raw surge of sorcery is bound to the humbling cadence of padded dependency. Every tantrum, every surge of wild energy, risks not only reshaping the battle?eld but also unraveling your composure. To walk this path is to accept that immense magical potential comes hand-in-hand with regression, vulnerability, and the ever-present crinkle of fate. Your choices will determine whether you are remembered as a chaotic liability, a resilient innovator, or a legend who turned weakness into doctrine.
Within hidden nurseries and arcane halls, others
like you wrestle with their dual nature. Some embrace the chaos of plushie storms and baby-brained confusion, others codify their origins into strict doctrine, weaving resilience from regression. Institutions may seek to regulate your tantrums, allies may rally to your cause, and enemies may mock your dependency - but only you can decide how to wield this peculiar inheritance. The world awaits to see what kind of sorcerer you will become.

For use with any fantasy roleplaying ruleset. Play the best game of your life!

spells.name: Sudden Outfit

components.material: a doll’s dress and a single thread

spells.description:
You attempt to force a creature you can see within range to don a ridiculous outfit over their current clothing and armor. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, it is instantly adorned in a frilly, brightly colored, and completely inappropriate outfit of your design for the duration. While the outfit is harmless, it is incredibly distracting and humiliating. The target has disadvantage on Charisma (Intimidation) and Charisma (Persuasion) checks for the duration. As a bonus action on your subsequent turns, you can change the outfit’s color or style.  
Mundane Makeover 3rd-level transmutation

spells.name: Suggestion Box

components.material: a small empty box and a slip of paper

spells.description: You touch a small container, turning it into a magical suggestion box. For the duration, any creature that can write can place a note inside with a suggestion for a course of action. When you open the box, you magically know who wrote each suggestion. Furthermore, any creature that writes a suggestion must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or also magically imbue the note with a secret they are trying to keep, which you learn upon reading it.

spells.name: Time-Out Corner
spells.description: You attempt to banish a creature to a harmless demiplane. Choose one creature you can see within range. The target must succeed on a Charisma saving throw or be teleported to a small, featureless room that contains only a single wooden stool in the corner. For the duration, the creature is incapacitated and trapped. At the end of each of its turns, the target can repeat the saving throw, ending the effect on a success and reappearing in the space it left or the nearest unoccupied space.
